title: Check yourself: Managed Agents: Anthropic runs the agent

questions.stem: A team needs an agent to run a task for several hours, survive restarts of its own service, and be resumed the next day, and it does not want to build a sandbox. Which option fits?

options.text: The Client SDK's tool runner, which hosts the sandbox for the loop
options.says: Ruled out because the page says the tool runner "drives the same kind of loop inside your process and hosts nothing", while the sandbox belongs to the hosted product.

options.text: The Messages API alone, which stores the conversation for each request
options.says: Ruled out because the Messages API is "Direct model prompting access", for "Custom agent loops and fine-grained control", and you keep the history yourself.

options.text: The Claude Code CLI, started again by hand each morning
options.says: Ruled out because the CLI is something you drive yourself: "You use the CLI by hand."

options.text: The hosted harness, which stores sessions on Anthropic's side
options.says: The overview table gives "Long-running tasks and asynchronous work" as the best fit, and says sessions "resume cleanly after pauses" with history and outputs stored server-side, so your service holds only an ID.

origin.section: Two ways to build, and the SDK in between

questions.stem: A session is created with a tools override that names one tool, while the saved agent lists eight. What does the session have?

options.text: Only that lone entry, with nothing else carried over
options.says: The page says "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration, so a `tools` override must list every tool the session should have."

options.text: The entry together with the agent's eight, merged into one list
options.says: Ruled out because "Overrides never merge with the agent's configuration", so nothing is added to the entry.

options.text: The agent's eight, which an override cannot remove
options.says: Ruled out because "overrides replace and never merge", so the agent's own list is not kept beside the entry.

options.text: None, until the agent is updated to a new version
options.says: Ruled out because "They apply to that one session, and the agent resource and its version are untouched.", so nothing waits for a new agent version.

origin.section: An agent is a versioned resource

questions.stem: A compliance team requires Zero Data Retention for every Claude workload. What follows for Managed Agents?

options.text: It qualifies once the sandbox runs on the team's own network
options.says: Ruled out because "Self-hosted sandboxes keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side but move tool execution into infrastructure you control", so the session data still sits with Anthropic.

options.text: It qualifies, since ZDR covers every endpoint of the API
options.says: Ruled out because the overview says "Managed Agents is not currently eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) coverage", not that it is covered.

options.text: It is ineligible today, since sessions store history server-side
options.says: The overview says sessions "store conversation history, sandbox state, and outputs server-side", so they are held on Anthropic's side.

options.text: It qualifies once the sessions have been deleted afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because "You can delete sessions and files through the API, but the data exists on Anthropic's side first", so deletion does not make it qualify.
